title: Denisovans
summary: Denisovans were an archaic human population first identified in 2010 from DNA of a finger bone found in Denisova Cave in the Altai Mountains of Siberia. A sister group to Neanderthals, they occupied the cave from at least 200,000 years ago until about 50,000 years ago, and some modern populations, such as Melanesians, carry their DNA.

uncertainty.note: Dates are for the Denisova Cave occupation; the species range across Asia is not established here. Years ago converted to year numbers without a 1950 adjustment (error far smaller than the uncertainty).

as_recorded.calendar: Years ago, radiocarbon and luminescence dating
as_recorded.value: occupied the cave from at least 200,000 years ago; disappeared around 50,000 years ago

when.display: from at least 200,000 to about 50,000 years ago

where.historical_name: Denisova Cave, Altai foothills, southern Siberia; no polities at this date

importance.justification: The first archaic human group defined from DNA alone, it reshaped understanding of human evolution and interbreeding.

sources.title: New Studies Reveal Deep History of Denisovans and Neanderthals in Southern Siberia
sources.publisher: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History

sources.title: Denisovans: Fossils reveal secrets about mysterious humans
